cell_or_location: cell 16 FGSM function, loss = criterion(pred, label)
error_message: Expected floating point type for target with class probabilities, got Long
what_user_was_trying: Implement an FGSM attack on one MNIST image by taking the image gradient with respect to CrossEntropyLoss and then perturbing the image in the gradient-sign direction.
real_cause: The FGSM cell fed model(img).argmax(axis=1) into cross_entropy. That converts the model output from raw logits of shape [1, 10] into a predicted class index of shape [1], so cross_entropy no longer receives differentiable class scores. PyTorch then interprets the input/target contract incorrectly and raises an error about target type for class probabilities.
user_diagnosis_steps: Reread the saved FGSM cell, printed pred.shape and label.shape, and noticed that pred had collapsed to torch.Size([1]) because argmax was applied before the loss instead of after it.
user_fix: Removed .argmax(axis=1) from the loss path, so cross_entropy now receives the raw model logits and the label stays as a class-index tensor.
memory_rule: For CrossEntropyLoss, pass raw logits into the loss and apply argmax only for reporting or final prediction. If argmax happens before the loss, you destroy the class-score information and break the gradient path needed for training or attacks.
next_drill: For the next classifier or adversarial notebook, print logits.shape, logits[0], label.shape, and label.dtype immediately before the loss call, then compute predicted_class = logits.argmax(dim=1) in a separate line after the loss input contract is verified.

error_message: Expected 2D array, got 1D array instead: array=[6. 0. 0. ... 2. 7. 1.]. Reshape your data either using array.reshape(-1, 1) if your data has a single feature or array.reshape(1, -1) if it contains a single sample.
what_user_was_trying: Train the first LogisticRegression baseline on sklearn load_digits data after creating a shared train/test split and a StandardScaler.
real_cause: The code applies scaler.transform(y_train), but StandardScaler was fitted on X_train with 64 feature columns and y_train is a 1D label vector. The code also reshapes scaler.transform(X_train) to (1, -1), collapsing all training rows into one giant sample instead of keeping the matrix shaped [n_samples, 64]. Labels should not be scaled for classification.
user_diagnosis_steps: Open: saved traceback points to model.fit(scaler.transform(X_train).reshape(1,-1), scaler.transform(y_train).reshape(1, -1)). The split output shows X_train has shape (1437, 64) and y_train has shape (1437,), so the model should receive a 2D feature matrix and a 1D label vector.
memory_rule: In sklearn classification, scale X features only and keep y as class labels. Do not reshape a full training matrix to (1, -1); estimators expect X shaped [n_samples, n_features] and y shaped [n_samples].
next_drill: Before every sklearn fit call, print X_train_scaled.shape and y_train.shape. For load_digits logistic regression they should be (1437, 64) and (1437,), not (1, 91968) or (1, 1437).

exercise: Lesson 2 Classical ML - Guided One-Notebook Sprint
cell_or_location: cell 12, KMeans passed into evaluate_classifier
error_message: KMeans reported pca + k-means accuracy: 0.0028 while the commented LogisticRegression model works correctly.
what_user_was_trying: Run K-Means on the digits data and compare it in the same notebook after the supervised classifiers.
real_cause: The notebook sends KMeans into evaluate_classifier(model, name), but that helper is written for supervised classifiers: it fits with y_train, predicts on X_test, compares predictions directly to y_test, and draws a classifier confusion matrix. KMeans is unsupervised and its predicted cluster IDs are arbitrary labels, not digit class labels. Cluster 0 does not mean digit 0, so direct accuracy against y_test is meaningless and can be near zero even when clusters contain real structure.
user_diagnosis_steps: Read the saved notebook: LogisticRegression, k-NN, SVM, and DecisionTreeClassifier work through evaluate_classifier because they learn from y_train. The KMeans cell uses model = KMeans(...) and then evaluate_classifier(model, "pca + k-means"), which applies the supervised evaluation path to an unsupervised clustering model.
memory_rule: Do not evaluate clustering with the same helper as supervised classifiers. KMeans cluster IDs are invented group names; visualize clusters or map each cluster to its majority true label before computing a label-based score.
next_drill: Create a separate evaluate_kmeans function that fits KMeans on X_pca or scaled X, plots points colored by cluster ID, and optionally builds a cluster-to-majority-digit table before any accuracy-like score.

exercise: Romania ONIA Steam price prediction P1
cell_or_location: cell 6, unique_gernes_count = np.array([i.split(",") for i in train_df["Genres"]])
error_message: setting an array element with a sequence. The requested array has an inhomogeneous shape after 1 dimensions. The detected shape was (3000,) + inhomogeneous part.
what_user_was_trying: Complete P1 by counting unique genres after splitting the comma-separated Genres column in the Steam price dataset.
real_cause: Each row can have a different number of comma-separated genre tags, so i.split(",") returns lists of different lengths. np.array tries to force those variable-length lists into a rectangular numeric-like array, but the result is ragged and NumPy raises a shape error. For this requirement the goal is a set of individual tags, not a 2D array.
user_diagnosis_steps: Saved traceback pointed directly to the np.array call on split Genres values. Earlier prints showed Samples, Average Price, and Average Owners already executed before the genre-count line failed. The saved notebook now loops through the Genres column, splits each row by comma, appends individual tags to a flat list, and then counts np.unique on that flat list.
user_fix: Flattened the split genre tags into one list before counting unique values, producing Unique Genres = 16.
memory_rule: When splitting a multi-label text column, expect variable-length lists. Flatten into a Python list or set before counting unique labels; do not force ragged split results into a NumPy array.
next_drill: On the next CSV task with comma-separated labels, inspect train_df["Genres"].head(), split one sample, then build a set of tags and print its sorted contents before using the count in an output file.

exercise: Romania ONIA Steam price prediction P2
cell_or_location: cell 8, model.fit(X, y) as final expression in notebook cell
error_message: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9c in position 2951: character maps to <undefined>
what_user_was_trying: Fit a RandomForestRegressor on numeric Steam price features after building X from owners, Metacritic score, Recommendations, Positive, and Negative.
real_cause: The traceback comes from sklearn's notebook HTML representation path, not from the feature matrix or target values. After model.fit(X, y), Jupyter tries to display the fitted estimator as an HTML diagram. sklearn reads estimator.js without specifying UTF-8, so Windows uses the Greek cp1253 codec and fails on a byte in that JavaScript file. The model fitting likely completed; the display hook failed.
user_diagnosis_steps: Saved traceback pointed into sklearn.utils._repr_html.estimator.estimator_html_repr and then Python's cp1253 decoder while reading estimator.js. The updated notebook now ends model.fit(X_train, y_train) with a semicolon, then computes predictions and prints validation MAE without the display traceback.
user_fix: Added a semicolon after model.fit(X_train, y_train) so Jupyter does not try to render the fitted sklearn estimator as an HTML diagram.
memory_rule: If sklearn fit finishes but the traceback is in _repr_html or estimator_html_repr, suspect notebook display rendering. Assign the fitted model or end the cell with a semicolon/print statement instead of relying on rich estimator display.
next_drill: In the next sklearn notebook cell, run model.fit(X, y); then print a simple confirmation such as type(model).__name__ or model.score/MAE, so Jupyter does not need to render the estimator diagram.

memory_rule: For BCEWithLogitsLoss, enforce both contracts at the same time: prediction and target shapes must match exactly, and targets must be float 0.0/1.0 rather than Long class indices. Preserve the batch dimension when flattening CNN features.
next_drill: On the next PyTorch binary classifier, run one batch before training and print batch_x.shape, model(batch_x).shape, batch_y.shape, and batch_y.dtype immediately before the loss.

exercise: IOAI 2024 Help BOBAI - 7-way classifier around frozen 5-way classifier
cell_or_location: cells 5, 8, and 12: uncertain_inputs filtering, SevenWayClassifier.__call__, and F1 evaluation
error_message: Notebook evaluates on labels > 4 only and still uses random fallback logic, so it does not solve the full 7-way classification contract.
what_user_was_trying: Extend the fixed 5-way neural classifier to handle labels 0-6 by detecting whether an embedding belongs to one of the new classes and otherwise passing it to the base classifier.
real_cause: The saved notebook filters to uncertain_inputs = inputs[labels > 4], which only tests classes 5 and 6. That hides the real routing problem: every sample must first be classified as old group 0-4 versus new class 5 versus new class 6. The current __call__ also keeps random class selection, so F1 on the filtered subset is not a valid full-task signal.
user_diagnosis_steps: Read the task constraints and inspected the saved cells: labels have all seven classes, but evaluation was run only on uncertain_inputs/uncertain_labels. The proposed strategy should be reframed as a distance/KNN/prototype router followed by the frozen base classifier for old-class samples.
memory_rule: For wrapper-classifier tasks, evaluate the full end-to-end contract, not only the hard subset. Build a router for old-vs-new first; only call the frozen base model when the router says the sample belongs to the old 0-4 group.
next_drill: Create a train/dev split over all 2473 examples, map labels to router targets old=0, class5=1, class6=2, then report macro F1 for the final 7-way predictions after routing plus base-classifier fallback.

exercise: IOAI 2024 Help BOBAI - 3-way router plus frozen 5-way classifier
cell_or_location: cells 8, 9, 11, and 16: router target mapping, router score, SevenWayClassifier.__call__, and macro F1
error_message: The updated router predicts values 0, 1, 2, but __call__ maps new-class predictions with pred.item() + 5, producing invalid class 7 for router output 2. Saved predictions contain 7.0 and macro F1 dropped to 0.5937.
what_user_was_trying: Fix the earlier binary old-vs-new router by making the router distinguish old group, class 5, and class 6.
real_cause: The router target was changed to three classes, but the output-to-final-label mapping was not updated consistently. For a router where 0 means old, 1 means class 5, and 2 means class 6, the final new-class label should be router_pred + 4, not router_pred + 5. The notebook also computes router accuracy by comparing 3-class router predictions against the old binary uncertain_mask, so that score is not meaningful.
user_diagnosis_steps: Inspected the saved notebook after the change. Cell 8 prints router labels with max 2.0. Cell 16 output includes predictions such as 7.0, which is outside the valid label set 0-6. The model score in cell 9 compares preds to uncertain_mask instead of the 3-class router target. User recognized it as an indexing-like offset error.
user_fix: Changed the inverse mapping for new-class router outputs so router class 1 maps to final label 5 and router class 2 maps to final label 6, instead of producing label 7. User reported good accuracy after the offset fix.
memory_rule: When you change an intermediate label encoding, update every downstream inverse mapping and metric to match it. Always print sorted unique final predictions before trusting F1; for this task they must be a subset of [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6], never 7.
next_drill: After fitting the router, print unique router labels, unique router predictions, unique final predictions, and compute two separate metrics: router accuracy against the 3-class router target, then final macro F1 against the original 0-6 labels.

exercise: CEOAI 2026 Practice Round 2 - Trace Twins
cell_or_location: cell 5 Submission.score_A and cell 9 local evaluation
error_message: setting an array element with a sequence; later clarified as could not broadcast input array from shape (200,7) into shape (7,)
what_user_was_trying: Create TF-IDF representations for trace windows and score whether each supplied pair came from the same program.
real_cause: The code fitted TF-IDF separately to one window represented as a list of 200 tokens, so sklearn treated those tokens as 200 separate documents and returned a matrix shaped (200, vocabulary_size). That matrix was then assigned to one row or scalar slot with an incompatible shape. The destination was also sized using the number of pairs instead of the number of windows.
user_diagnosis_steps: Inspected windows as a (12, 200) structure and established that rows are windows while columns are token positions. Printed the transform result and saw shape (200, 7), then distinguished the original windows matrix from the desired TF-IDF matrix with one row per complete window.
user_fix: Joined each 200-token window into one document string, fitted TfidfVectorizer once across the full corpus, then used each pair's window indices to select two TF-IDF rows and appended their dot product as the pair score. Saved local evaluation now reports Part A AUC 1.000 and 50.0/50.
memory_rule: For text similarity, define the document boundary before vectorizing. Here one complete 200-command window is one document, so TF-IDF must have shape [number_of_windows, vocabulary_size], and the returned score list must have one float per pair.
next_drill: Implement a Part B representation that ignores token identity and compare paired windows using renaming-invariant statistics such as sorted token frequencies, repetition patterns, or run-length features; validate Part B AUC separately.

exercise: CEOAI 2026 Practice Round 1 - Star Observatory
cell_or_location: Subtask 1 center prediction loop converting flat argmax index to coordinates
error_message: Initial center coordinates were computed with 128 - idx%128 and 128 - idx//128, flipping the image coordinate system.
what_user_was_trying: Convert the brightest pixel's flattened index into an (x, y) coordinate for the star center prediction subtask.
real_cause: The flat index from argmax already maps to row-major coordinates as x = idx % width and y = idx // width. Subtracting from 128 mirrored the coordinates and produced large avoidable errors.
user_diagnosis_steps: Compared predicted centers against the local test_hidden centers and saw systematic wrong coordinates. The corrected loop printed coordinates close to the hidden centers and achieved mean absolute coordinate error about 0.619 on the fixture.
user_fix: Changed the mapping to cords = np.array((idx % 128, idx // 128)) when converting argmax to star-center coordinates.
memory_rule: For a flattened HxW image index in row-major order, x is idx % W and y is idx // W. Do not mirror coordinates unless the statement defines a different origin.
next_drill: For the next image task, pick one known pixel coordinate, flatten it with y*W+x, then recover it with idx%W and idx//W before using that mapping in predictions.
